{{Short description|Relation with zero attributes}}
{{refimprove|date=December 2022}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''nullary relation''', '''0-ary relation''', or '''relation of degree zero'''  is a [[Finitary relation|relation]] with [[nullary|zero attributes]].  There are exactly two relations of degree zero.  One has [[cardinality]] zero; that is, contains no [[tuple]]s at all.  The other has cardinality 1 and contains only the unique 0-tuple.<ref name="db-in-depth">{{cite book |last1=Date |first1=Christopher J.|authorlink = Christopher J. Date |title=Database In Depth |date=May 2005 |publisher=O'Reilly |location=Sebastopol, California |isbn=978-0-596-10012-4 |edition=1}}</ref><sup>:56</sup>

The zero-degree relations represent true and false in [[relational algebra]].<ref name="db-in-depth" /><sup>:57</sup>  Under the [[closed-world assumption]], an ''n''-ary relation is interpreted as the [[Extension (semantics)|extension]] of some ''n''-adic [[predicate (mathematical logic)|predicate]]: all and only those ''n''-tuples whose values, substituted for corresponding [[free variable]]s in the predicate, yield [[proposition]]s that hold true, appear in the relation.  A zero-degree relation is therefore interpreted as the extension of the 0-adic predicate {{math|''P''() → true}}.  The zero-degree relation with cardinality zero therefore represents false because it contains no tuples that yield a true proposition, and the zero-degree relation with cardinality 1 represents true because it contains the unique 0-tuple that yields a true proposition.

The zero-degree relations are also significant as [[identity element|identities]] for certain operators in the relational algebra.  The zero-degree relation of cardinality 1 is the identity with respect to [[natural join|join]] (⋈); that is, when it is joined with any other relation {{math|''R''}}, the result is {{math|''R''}}.  Defining an identity with respect to join makes it possible to extend the [[binary operator|binary]] join operator into a ''n''-ary join operator.<ref name="db-in-depth" /><sup>:89</sup>

Since the relational [[Relational_algebra#Set_operators|Cartesian product]] is a special case of join, the zero-degree relation of cardinality 1 is also the identity with respect to the Cartesian product.<ref name="db-in-depth" /><sup>:89</sup>

A [[projection (relational algebra)|projection]] of a relation over no attributes yields one of the relations of degree zero. If the projected relation has cardinality 0, the projection will have cardinality 0; if the projected relation has positive cardinality, the result will have cardinality 1.

[[Hugh Darwen]] refers to the zero-degree relation with cardinality 0 as TABLE_DUM and the relation with cardinality 1 as TABLE_DEE, alluding to the characters [[Tweedledum and Tweedledee]].<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia|first=Hugh|last=Darwen|editor1-last=Date|editor1-first=C. J.|editor2-last=Darwen|editor2-first=Hugh|title=The Nullologist in Relationland|encyclopedia=Relational Database Writings 1989–1991|year=1992|publisher=Addison-Wesley|location=Reading, Massachusetts}}</ref>
